references.text: Describes how the Egyptians pursued the Israelites with horses, chariots, and horsemen, expanding on Pharaoh's military strength mentioned in verse 7.
Mentions again Pharaoh's chariots, horsemen, and all his army, referring back to the forces gathered in verse 7.
The Egyptians pursued with all of Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen into the sea, referencing the forces described in verse 7.
The water returned and covered the chariots and horsemen, the entire army of Pharaoh. This shows the fate of the forces from verse 7.
Moses' song mentions that Pharaoh's chariots and army were cast into the sea, referring to the destruction of the forces gathered in 14:7.
Moses reminds the Israelites how the Lord caused the waters of the Red Sea to sweep over the Egyptian army, horses, and chariots.
Joshua reminds the people that the Egyptians pursued their ancestors with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.
The psalm praises the Lord who overthrew Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, referring to the events in Exodus 14.
Mentions שָׁלִישִׁים (officers/commanders) in connection with royal chariots, the same term used in Exodus 14:7.
Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, with 1,400 chariots. This shows Egyptian military chariot power as background for Pharaoh's forces.
A contrasting parallel between Egypt's military might that pursues (Exodus) and that which punishes God's people (2 Chronicles).
Theological contrast between the enemy's proud use of chariots (Exodus) and David's strategic destruction of them to show trust in God.
